subtitle.en: Saying no, listening to no and asking for help

hook.en: Your voice is a tool. You can use it to say no, to ask a question and to get help.
hook.hg: Tumhari awaaz ek tool hai. Isse tum 'no' bol sakte ho, sawaal pooch sakte ho aur help maang sakte ho.

objectives.en: Say no in a clear voice when something feels wrong.
objectives.hg: Jab kuch galat lage toh clear awaaz mein 'no' bol sako.

objectives.en: Stop when another person says no.
objectives.hg: Jab koi doosra 'no' bole toh ruk sako.

objectives.en: Ask questions and tell a grown-up you trust when you need help.
objectives.hg: Sawaal pooch sako aur help chahiye ho toh kisi bharose wale bade ko bata sako.

body.en: Your body belongs to you. If a touch, a game or a dare feels bad or scary, you can say no. Look at the person and say, 'No. I don't like that.' Then move away to a grown-up you trust. You can say no to a child or to a grown-up. Saying no to something unsafe is not rude.
body.hg: Tumhari body tumhari apni hai. Agar koi touch, koi game ya koi dare bura ya scary lage, toh tum 'no' bol sakte ho. Us insaan ki taraf dekho aur bolo, 'Nahi. Mujhe yeh pasand nahi.' Phir wahan se hat ke kisi bharose wale bade ke paas jao. Tum 'no' kisi bacche ko bhi bol sakte ho aur kisi bade ko bhi. Kisi unsafe cheez ko 'no' bolna rude nahi hai.

h.en: When someone says no, we stop
h.hg: Jab koi 'no' bole, toh hum ruk jaate hain

body.en: Other children have a voice too. If your friend says 'Stop' or 'I don't want to play', you stop right away. You do not push, tease or ask again and again. You can say, 'Okay.' Listening to someone's no shows that you are a good friend.
body.hg: Doosre bacchon ki bhi apni awaaz hai. Agar tumhara dost bole 'Ruko' ya 'Mujhe nahi khelna', toh tum turant ruk jaate ho. Tum zor nahi daalte, chidhate nahi aur baar-baar nahi poochte. Tum bol sakte ho, 'Okay.' Kisi ki 'no' sunna dikhata hai ki tum achhe dost ho.

body.en: Nobody knows everything. Asking is how we learn. You can ask, 'What does this word mean?' or 'Why is my body like this?' No question about your body or your feelings is silly or dirty. If one grown-up does not know the answer, you can ask another one.
body.hg: Sab kuch kisi ko nahi pata hota. Poochkar hi hum seekhte hain. Tum pooch sakte ho, 'Is word ka kya matlab hai?' ya 'Meri body aisi kyun hai?' Apni body ya apni feelings ke baare mein koi bhi sawaal silly ya ganda nahi hota. Agar ek bade ko answer na pata ho, toh tum kisi doosre bade se pooch sakte ho.

h.hg: Kisi bharose wale bade ko batao

body.en: If something makes you feel scared, sad or mixed up, tell a grown-up you trust, like mummy, papa, dadi or a teacher. Say, 'I need help. Something happened.' If they do not listen, tell another grown-up. Keep telling until someone helps. If you could not say no, it is not your fault. You will not be in trouble for telling.
body.hg: Agar kisi baat se tumhe darr lage, dukh ho ya confusion ho, toh kisi bharose wale bade ko batao, jaise mummy, papa, dadi ya teacher. Bolo, 'Mujhe help chahiye. Kuch hua hai.' Agar woh na sunein, toh kisi doosre bade ko batao. Tab tak batate raho jab tak koi help na kare. Agar tum 'no' nahi bol paaye, tab bhi yeh tumhari galti nahi hai. Batane pe tumhe daant nahi padegi.

claim.en: Good children always say yes to grown-ups.
claim.hg: Achhe bacche badon ki har baat pe hamesha 'haan' bolte hain.

fact.en: Good children listen and are polite, but they can still say no to anything that feels unsafe, hurts them or must be kept secret. Then they tell a trusted adult.
fact.hg: Achhe bacche baat sunte hain aur polite rehte hain, par woh aisi har cheez ko 'no' bol sakte hain jo unsafe lage, jisse hurt ho ya jise secret rakhne ko bola jaye. Phir woh kisi trusted bade ko batate hain.

takeaways.en: You can say no to anything that feels wrong or unsafe.
takeaways.hg: Jo bhi cheez galat ya unsafe lage, use tum 'no' bol sakte ho.

takeaways.en: When someone else says no or stop, you stop.
takeaways.hg: Jab koi doosra 'no' ya 'ruko' bole, toh tum ruk jaate ho.

takeaways.en: Keep telling trusted grown-ups until one of them helps you.
takeaways.hg: Bharose wale badon ko tab tak batate raho jab tak unme se koi tumhari help na kare.

activity.en: Practise with a parent or in front of a mirror. Say 'No, I don't like that' and 'I need help' in a loud, clear voice three times each. Then name three grown-ups you can tell.
activity.hg: Parents ke saath ya mirror ke saamne practice karo. 'Nahi, mujhe yeh pasand nahi' aur 'Mujhe help chahiye' ko loud, clear awaaz mein teen-teen baar bolo. Phir aise teen badon ke naam batao jinhe tum bata sakte ho.

q.en: An uncle you know wants a hug, but you do not feel like it. What can you do?
q.hg: Ek jaan-pehchaan ke uncle tumhe hug karna chahte hain, par tumhara mann nahi hai. Tum kya kar sakte ho?

options.en: Hug him anyway so that he is not upset
options.hg: Phir bhi hug kar lo taaki unhe bura na lage

options.en: Run and hide without telling anyone
options.hg: Kisi ko bataye bina bhaag ke chhup jao

options.en: Say 'No, thank you' and do namaste or wave instead
options.hg: Bolo 'No, thank you' aur uski jagah namaste karo ya haath hilao

explain.en: You decide who hugs you. A polite no with a namaste or a wave is respectful and keeps you comfortable.
explain.hg: Tumhe kaun hug kare, yeh tum decide karte ho. Namaste ya wave ke saath polite 'no' respectful bhi hai aur tum comfortable bhi rehte ho.

q.en: If the first grown-up does not listen, you should stop asking for help.
q.hg: Agar pehla bada tumhari baat na sune, toh tumhe help maangna band kar dena chahiye.

options.en: True
options.hg: Sahi

options.en: False
options.hg: Galat

explain.en: Tell another trusted grown-up, and keep telling until someone helps you.
explain.hg: Kisi doosre bharose wale bade ko batao, aur tab tak batate raho jab tak koi tumhari help na kare.

title.en: Say It Clearly: Feelings, Fights and Awkward Talks
title.hg: Seedha Bolo: Feelings, Fights aur Awkward Baatein

subtitle.en: 'I' sentences, saying no to friends, talking to parents and teachers, and fixing a fight
subtitle.hg: 'Main' wale sentences, doston ko 'no' bolna, parents aur teachers se baat karna, aur fight sort karna

hook.en: Most fights are not really about the pencil box. They happen because nobody says what they actually feel.
hook.hg: Zyadatar fights asal mein pencil box ke baare mein nahi hoti. Woh isliye hoti hain kyunki koi yeh nahi bolta ki use sach mein kya feel ho raha hai.

objectives.en: Use an 'I' sentence to say what bothers you without blaming.
objectives.hg: 'Main' wale sentence se bina blame kiye bata sako ki tumhe kya pareshaan kar raha hai.

objectives.en: Say no to a friend, and accept a friend's no.
objectives.hg: Dost ko 'no' bol sako, aur dost ki 'no' accept kar sako.

objectives.en: Start an awkward conversation with a parent or teacher, and repair a fight.
objectives.hg: Parent ya teacher se awkward baat shuru kar sako, aur fight repair kar sako.

body.en: When something bothers you, blaming usually starts a fight: 'You always make fun of me!' An 'I' sentence works better because it talks about your feeling, not the other person's character. Use three parts: I feel, when, I need. 'I feel bad when you call me that name. I need you to use my real name.' Or: 'I feel left out when you two whisper. Can I join?' Say it in a normal voice, face to face, when both of you are calm. It will feel strange the first few times. It still works.
body.hg: Jab koi baat tumhe pareshaan karti hai, toh blame karne se usually fight shuru ho jaati hai: 'Tu hamesha mera mazaak udata hai!' 'Main' wala sentence better kaam karta hai kyunki woh tumhari feeling ki baat karta hai, saamne wale ke character ki nahi. Iske teen parts hain: mujhe feel hota hai, jab, mujhe chahiye. 'Jab tum mujhe us naam se bulate ho toh mujhe bura lagta hai. Mujhe chahiye ki tum mera asli naam lo.' Ya: 'Jab tum dono kaana-phoosi karte ho toh mujhe left out feel hota hai. Main bhi aa jaun?' Isse normal awaaz mein, face to face, tab bolo jab dono calm hon. Pehli kuch baar ajeeb lagega. Phir bhi yeh kaam karta hai.

body.en: Friends sometimes push: copy my homework, skip class, take this dare, tell me her secret. A real no is short, clear and repeated. 'No, I'm not doing that.' You do not need a long excuse. If they push again, say the same line again and offer something else: 'No. Let's play football instead.' If they call you boring or a baby, that is pressure, not friendship. Walk away if you need to. And when a friend says no to you, treat it exactly the way you want yours treated: accept it the first time.
body.hg: Dost kabhi-kabhi push karte hain: mera homework copy kar lo, class bunk karo, yeh dare lo, uska secret mujhe bata do. Asli 'no' short, clear aur repeated hoti hai. 'Nahi, mujhe yeh nahi karna.' Lambe excuse ki zaroorat nahi. Agar woh phir push karein, toh wahi line phir se bolo aur kuch aur offer karo: 'Nahi. Chalo iski jagah football khelte hain.' Agar woh tumhe boring ya baccha bolein, toh woh pressure hai, dosti nahi. Zaroorat pade toh wahan se chale jao. Aur jab koi dost tumhe 'no' bole, toh uske saath waisa hi karo jaisa tum apni 'no' ke saath chahte ho: pehli baar mein hi maan lo.

h.en: Awkward talks with parents and teachers
h.hg: Parents aur teachers se awkward baatein

body.en: Adults were your age once, and most would rather be asked than kept in the dark. Choose a quiet moment, not when they are rushing to work or angry. Start with a line that prepares them: 'Mumma, I want to ask something and I feel a bit shy.' or 'Sir, can I talk to you after class? Something is bothering me.' If speaking is hard, write a note or a message. Say what happened, how you feel and what you need. If the first adult scolds or brushes it off, try another: a grandparent, an aunt, a teacher or the school counsellor.
body.hg: Bade bhi kabhi tumhari age ke the, aur zyadatar yahi chahenge ki unse poocha jaye, na ki baat chhupayi jaye. Koi quiet moment choose karo, tab nahi jab woh kaam ke liye bhaag rahe hon ya gusse mein hon. Aisi line se start karo jo unhe ready kar de: 'Mumma, mujhe kuch poochna hai aur thodi sharam aa rahi hai.' ya 'Sir, kya class ke baad aapse baat ho sakti hai? Ek cheez mujhe pareshaan kar rahi hai.' Agar bolna mushkil lage, toh ek note ya message likh do. Batao ki kya hua, tumhe kaisa lag raha hai aur tumhe kya chahiye. Agar pehla adult daant de ya baat taal de, toh kisi aur ko try karo: dada-dadi, mausi, koi teacher ya school counsellor.

body.en: Disagreements are normal, even between best friends. First, cool down: breathe slowly, drink water, wait until your body feels calm. Second, listen to their side without interrupting and repeat it back: 'So you felt I ignored you.' Third, say your side with an 'I' sentence. Fourth, own your part: a real sorry names what you did, like 'Sorry I shared your secret', without adding 'but'. Fifth, agree on what will change. If someone is hitting, threatening or bullying, that is not an ordinary fight, and you should bring in an adult.
body.hg: Disagreements normal hain, best friends ke beech bhi. Pehla step, cool down: dheere saans lo, paani piyo, tab tak ruko jab tak body calm na lage. Doosra, beech mein toke bina unki side suno aur use repeat karke batao: 'Toh tumhe laga maine tumhe ignore kiya.' Teesra, apni side 'main' wale sentence se bolo. Chautha, apna part own karo: asli sorry mein woh cheez boli jaati hai jo tumne ki, jaise 'Sorry, maine tumhara secret bata diya', aur uske baad 'but' nahi lagaya jata. Paanchva, decide karo ki aage kya change hoga. Agar koi maar raha hai, dhamka raha hai ya bully kar raha hai, toh woh ordinary fight nahi hai, aur tumhe kisi adult ko beech mein lana chahiye.

claim.en: If I tell my parents about a problem, I will only get scolded, so it is better to hide it.
claim.hg: Agar main parents ko apni problem bataun toh bas daant padegi, isliye chhupana hi better hai.

fact.en: Some parents do react with worry or anger at first, but hidden problems usually grow. Most adults calm down and help. If one adult does not, another trusted adult can.
fact.hg: Kuch parents pehle worry ya gusse se react karte hain, par chhupayi hui problems usually badhti hi hain. Zyadatar adults calm hokar help karte hain. Agar ek adult help na kare, toh koi doosra trusted adult kar sakta hai.

takeaways.en: 'I feel... when... I need...' says what hurts without starting a fight.
takeaways.hg: 'Mujhe feel hota hai... jab... mujhe chahiye...' bina fight shuru kiye bata deta hai ki kya hurt kar raha hai.

takeaways.en: A good no is short and repeated, and a friend's no is accepted the first time.
takeaways.hg: Achhi 'no' short aur repeated hoti hai, aur dost ki 'no' pehli baar mein accept ki jaati hai.

takeaways.en: Cool down, listen, speak, apologise for your part and agree on a change.
takeaways.hg: Cool down karo, suno, apni baat bolo, apne part ke liye sorry bolo aur change pe agree karo.

activity.en: Write three 'I' sentences for real situations from this week, using 'I feel... when... I need...'. Pick the easiest one and say it to the person tomorrow.
activity.hg: Is week ki real situations ke liye teen 'main' wale sentences likho, 'Mujhe feel hota hai... jab... mujhe chahiye...' use karke. Sabse easy wala choose karo aur kal us insaan ko bol do.

q.en: You are furious with a friend. What is the best first step?
q.hg: Tumhe ek dost pe bahut gussa aa raha hai. Best first step kya hai?

options.en: Take time to calm down before you talk
options.hg: Baat karne se pehle calm hone ke liye time lo

options.en: Tell everyone in class what they did
options.hg: Class mein sabko bata do ki usne kya kiya

options.en: Send an angry message right now
options.hg: Abhi ek angry message bhej do

options.en: Stop talking to them for good
options.hg: Usse hamesha ke liye baat karna band kar do

explain.en: Angry words are hard to take back. Calming down first lets you say what you really mean.
explain.hg: Gusse mein bole words wapas lena mushkil hota hai. Pehle calm hone se tum woh bol paate ho jo sach mein bolna chahte ho.

q.en: Tara wants to ask her mother about a change in her body but feels shy. Which opening is most likely to work?
q.hg: Tara apni body mein aaye ek change ke baare mein mummy se poochna chahti hai, par use sharam aa rahi hai. Kaun-sa opening sabse zyada kaam karega?

options.en: Say 'Nothing, forget it' when her mother asks
options.hg: Jab mummy poochein toh bol de 'Kuch nahi, chhodo'

options.en: 'Mumma, I have a question and I feel a bit shy. Can we talk tonight?'
options.hg: 'Mumma, mujhe ek sawaal poochna hai aur thodi sharam aa rahi hai. Aaj raat baat kar sakte hain?'

options.en: Wait for her mother to guess what is wrong
options.hg: Wait kare ki mummy khud guess kar lein ki kya baat hai

explain.en: Naming the shyness and asking for a time prepares her mother to listen. Adults cannot help with what they have to guess.
explain.hg: Apni sharam bata dene aur time maangne se mummy sunne ke liye ready ho jaati hain. Jis cheez ka adults ko guess karna pade, usme woh help nahi kar paate.

title.en: Your Call: Decisions, Pressure and Manipulation
title.hg: Faisla Tumhara: Decisions, Pressure aur Manipulation

subtitle.en: A method for decisions, the tricks people use to bend your no, and how to hold it
subtitle.hg: Decisions lene ka ek method, tumhari 'no' ko modne ke liye use hone wali tricks, aur uspe tike rehne ka tareeka

hook.en: If someone needs guilt, speed or secrecy to get your yes, it was never really your yes.
hook.hg: Agar kisi ko tumhari 'yes' paane ke liye guilt, jaldbaazi ya secrecy ka sahara lena pade, toh woh kabhi tumhari 'yes' thi hi nahi.

objectives.en: Use a step-by-step method for decisions that matter.
objectives.hg: Important decisions ke liye step-by-step method use kar sako.

objectives.en: Name common manipulation tactics when you hear them.
objectives.hg: Common manipulation tactics ko sunte hi pehchaan sako.

objectives.en: Say an assertive no, and respect another person's no.
objectives.hg: Assertive 'no' bol sako, aur doosre ki 'no' ko respect kar sako.

h.en: A method for decisions that matter

body.en: Quick choices like which snack to buy need no method. Bigger ones do: going to a party, sharing a photo, keeping a secret, getting into a relationship. Use five steps. Stop: do not answer while you are excited, scared or being rushed. Options: list at least three, including 'not now'. Outcomes: for each one, ask what could happen tomorrow, next month and next year. Values: which option fits the person you want to be, and the law? Decide, then review later. A useful test is to ask whether you would be comfortable if a person you respect knew about it.
body.hg: Kaun-sa snack lena hai jaise quick choices ke liye kisi method ki zaroorat nahi. Bade decisions ke liye hai: party mein jaana, photo share karna, koi secret rakhna, relationship mein aana. Paanch steps use karo. Stop: jab tum excited ho, dare hue ho ya tumse jaldi karayi ja rahi ho, tab answer mat do. Options: kam se kam teen likho, jisme 'abhi nahi' bhi ho. Outcomes: har option ke liye socho ki kal, agle mahine aur agle saal kya ho sakta hai. Values: kaun-sa option us insaan se match karta hai jo tum banna chahte ho, aur law se? Decide karo, phir baad mein review karo. Ek kaam ka test yeh poochna hai ki agar kisi aise insaan ko pata chale jiski tum respect karte ho, toh kya tum comfortable rahoge.

body.en: Manipulation is getting someone to do something by pressure or tricks instead of honest asking. Learn the common moves. Guilt: 'If you really cared, you would.' Bandwagon: 'Everyone does it.' Flattery with a hook: 'You're so mature, not like the others.' Rushing: 'Decide now or forget it.' Secrecy: 'Don't tell anyone, they won't understand.' Threats: 'I'll leave you', 'I'll tell people'. Gaslighting: 'That never happened, you're overreacting,' said to make you doubt your own memory. Persistent asking: the same request until you are too tired to refuse. One sign is common to all of them: your discomfort is treated as a problem to be removed, not a reason to stop.
body.hg: Manipulation matlab kisi se honestly poochne ki jagah pressure ya tricks se koi kaam karwana. Iske common moves pehchaan lo. Guilt: 'Agar tumhe sach mein parwah hoti, toh tum kar dete.' Bandwagon: 'Sab karte hain.' Hook wali tareef: 'Tum kitne mature ho, baakiyon jaise nahi.' Rushing: 'Abhi decide karo warna bhool jao.' Secrecy: 'Kisi ko mat batana, woh nahi samjhenge.' Threats: 'Main tumhe chhod dunga', 'Main sabko bata dunga'. Gaslighting: 'Aisa kabhi hua hi nahi, tum overreact kar rahe ho,' jo isliye bola jata hai ki tum apni hi memory pe doubt karne lago. Persistent asking: wahi request tab tak, jab tak tum mana karte-karte thak na jao. In sabme ek sign common hai: tumhari discomfort ko rukne ki wajah nahi, balki hatane layak problem maana jata hai.

body.en: An assertive no is calm, short and firm. It is not aggressive and it is not apologetic. Useful lines: 'No, I'm not comfortable with that.' 'I've decided, please stop asking.' 'I need time; if you need an answer now, it's no.' You do not owe an explanation, and explaining too much gives the other person points to argue with. If they continue, repeat the same sentence like a broken record, then leave or end the chat. You may change a yes to a no at any point. If a no is met with threats or blackmail, that is the moment to involve a trusted adult.
body.hg: Assertive 'no' calm, short aur firm hoti hai. Usme na aggression hota hai, na sorry wala tone. Kaam ki lines: 'Nahi, main isme comfortable nahi hoon.' 'Maine decide kar liya hai, please ab mat poocho.' 'Mujhe time chahiye; agar answer abhi chahiye, toh answer no hai.' Explanation dena tumhari zimmedari nahi hai, aur zyada explain karne se saamne wale ko argue karne ke points mil jaate hain. Agar woh continue karein, toh wahi sentence broken record ki tarah repeat karo, phir wahan se nikal jao ya chat band kar do. Tum kisi bhi point pe apni 'yes' ko 'no' mein badal sakte ho. Agar 'no' ke jawab mein dhamki ya blackmail mile, toh wahi moment hai kisi trusted adult ko involve karne ka.

body.en: The skill has a second half. When someone tells you no, to a date, a hug, a photo, a plan or a favour, the respectful reply is 'Okay, thanks for telling me.' Do not ask again in a different way, sulk, joke about it to others or go silent to punish them. Hesitation, 'maybe', 'I guess' and silence are not yes. A yes given after nagging is not a real yes either. Feeling hurt by a no is human. Handle that feeling with a friend, a walk or a journal, not by making the other person pay for it.
body.hg: Is skill ka ek second half bhi hai. Jab koi tumhe 'no' bole, chahe date ke liye, hug ke liye, photo ke liye, kisi plan ke liye ya kisi favour ke liye, toh respectful reply hai 'Okay, batane ke liye thanks.' Ghuma-phira ke dobara mat poocho, sulk mat karo, doosron ke saamne uska joke mat banao aur punish karne ke liye silent mat ho jao. Hesitation, 'maybe', 'dekhte hain' aur chuppi ka matlab 'yes' nahi hota. Zid karke nikalwayi gayi 'yes' bhi asli 'yes' nahi hai. 'No' sunke hurt hona human hai. Us feeling ko kisi dost ke saath, walk pe ya journal likhkar handle karo, saamne wale se uski keemat wasool karke nahi.

claim.en: Saying no makes you rude, and a good friend or partner never refuses.
claim.hg: 'No' bolna rude hai, aur achha dost ya partner kabhi mana nahi karta.

fact.en: A clear no is honest, and honesty is what healthy friendships and relationships run on. People who respect you accept your no. Someone who punishes you for refusing is showing you a warning sign about themselves.
fact.hg: Clear 'no' honesty hai, aur healthy dosti aur relationships honesty pe hi chalte hain. Jo log tumhari respect karte hain, woh tumhari 'no' accept kar lete hain. Jo mana karne pe tumhe punish karta hai, woh apne baare mein ek warning sign de raha hai.

takeaways.en: For big decisions: stop, list options, think through outcomes, check your values, decide and review.
takeaways.hg: Bade decisions ke liye: ruko, options likho, outcomes socho, apni values check karo, decide karo aur review karo.

takeaways.en: Guilt, rushing, secrecy, threats and repeated asking are manipulation, not persuasion.
takeaways.hg: Guilt, rushing, secrecy, threats aur baar-baar poochna manipulation hai, persuasion nahi.

takeaways.en: Your no needs no explanation, and other people's no deserves the same respect.
takeaways.hg: Tumhari 'no' ko kisi explanation ki zaroorat nahi, aur doosron ki 'no' bhi utni hi respect deserve karti hai.

activity.en: Write your personal 'no script': three sentences you could actually say when pressured, in the language you really speak. Practise them aloud once. Then write one sentence you will say when somebody else tells you no.
activity.hg: Apni personal 'no script' likho: teen aise sentences jo tum pressure mein sach mein bol sako, usi language mein jo tum actually bolte ho. Unhe ek baar zor se bolkar practice karo. Phir ek aisa sentence likho jo tum tab bologe jab koi aur tumhe 'no' bolega.

q.en: 'If you were really my friend, you would do this for me.' Which tactic is this?
q.hg: 'Agar tu sach mein mera dost hota, toh mere liye yeh kar deta.' Yeh kaun-si tactic hai?

options.en: Flattery
options.hg: Flattery (chaaplusi)

options.en: Guilt-tripping
options.hg: Guilt-tripping

options.en: Honest disagreement
options.hg: Honest disagreement

options.en: Gaslighting
options.hg: Gaslighting

explain.en: It turns your refusal into proof that you do not care, so that guilt does the persuading. Friendship is not measured by obedience.
explain.hg: Yeh tumhare mana karne ko is baat ka proof bana deti hai ki tumhe parwah nahi, taaki guilt tumse kaam karwa le. Dosti obedience se measure nahi hoti.

q.en: After saying yes to a plan, you are allowed to change your mind and say no.
q.hg: Kisi plan ko 'yes' bolne ke baad bhi tum apna mann badalkar 'no' bol sakte ho.

options.en: True
options.hg: Sahi

options.en: False
options.hg: Galat

explain.en: A yes is not a contract. New information or a change in how you feel is reason enough to say no.
explain.hg: 'Yes' koi contract nahi hai. Nayi information milna ya tumhari feeling ka badal jana 'no' bolne ke liye kaafi reason hai.

warning.en: If someone threatens you, blackmails you or pushes you for photos, meetings or secrecy, tell a trusted adult. You can also call 1098 (Child Helpline). For online threats or blackmail, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in.
warning.hg: Agar koi tumhe dhamki de, blackmail kare ya photos, milne ya secret rakhne ke liye pressure daale, toh kisi trusted adult ko batao. Tum 1098 (Child Helpline) pe bhi call kar sakte ho. Online dhamki ya blackmail ke liye 1930 pe call karo ya cybercrime.gov.in pe report karo.

title.en: Hard Conversations: Doctors, Parents and Friends in Trouble
title.hg: Mushkil Conversations: Doctor, Parents aur Mushkil Mein Dost

subtitle.en: What to say, what to ask and what you can expect
subtitle.hg: Kya bolein, kya poochein aur kya expect karein

hook.en: A doctor can only treat what you tell them. Half-truths get half-treatment.
hook.hg: Doctor sirf usi ka ilaaj kar sakte hain jo tum unhe batate ho. Aadha sach bataoge toh treatment bhi aadha milega.

objectives.en: Prepare for a medical appointment and ask the questions that matter.
objectives.hg: Doctor ke appointment ki taiyaari kar sako aur zaroori sawaal pooch sako.

objectives.en: Explain what confidentiality means and where its limits are, especially under 18.
objectives.hg: Samjha sako ki confidentiality ka kya matlab hai aur uski limits kahan hain, khaaskar 18 se kam age mein.

objectives.en: Open a difficult conversation with a parent and respond well when a friend confides in you.
objectives.hg: Parent se mushkil baat shuru kar sako aur jab koi dost apni baat share kare toh sahi tareeke se saath de sako.

h.hg: Doctor ke paas jaane ki taiyaari

body.en: Embarrassment makes people go blank in the clinic, so prepare. Before you go, write down what the problem is, when it started, what makes it better or worse, any medicines you take, and the date of your last period if you have periods. Use plain body words: penis, vulva, vagina, anus, breast. Doctors hear them all day. You can open with, 'This is awkward for me, but I need to ask about...' Where available, you may ask for a doctor of a particular gender, and for a family member or nurse to be present during an examination. Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics in government facilities are meant for young people's questions.
body.hg: Sharam ki wajah se clinic mein logon ka dimaag blank ho jata hai, isliye prepare karke jao. Jaane se pehle likh lo ki problem kya hai, kab shuru hui, kisse better ya worse hoti hai, tum kaun-si medicines lete ho, aur agar tumhe periods aate hain toh last period ki date. Body ke seedhe words use karo: penis, vulva, vagina, anus, breast. Doctors ye words din bhar sunte hain. Tum aise start kar sakte ho, 'Mujhe yeh bolne mein awkward lag raha hai, par mujhe is baare mein poochna hai...' Jahan available ho, tum kisi particular gender ke doctor ke liye bol sakte ho, aur examination ke time family member ya nurse ke present rehne ke liye bhi. Government facilities mein Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics (AFHC) young logon ke sawaalon ke liye hi bane hain.

h.en: Questions you have a right to ask
h.hg: Woh sawaal jo poochna tumhara right hai

body.en: Good care is a conversation, not a lecture. Ask until you understand: What do you think this is? What is this test or medicine for? How, and for how long, do I take it? What side effects should I watch for? What if it does not get better, and when should I come back? Is there another option? Repeat the plan in your own words to check it. Before any examination, the doctor should tell you what they are going to do and why, and you can ask them to pause or stop. Your responsibility is honesty: give the full history, including the parts you would rather skip.
body.hg: Achhi care ek conversation hai, lecture nahi. Jab tak samajh na aaye, poochte raho: Aapko kya lagta hai, yeh kya hai? Yeh test ya medicine kis liye hai? Isse kaise aur kitne din lena hai? Kin side effects pe nazar rakhun? Agar better na ho toh kya karun, aur dobara kab aaun? Kya koi aur option hai? Poora plan apne words mein repeat karke check kar lo ki tumne sahi samjha hai. Kisi bhi examination se pehle doctor ko tumhe batana chahiye ki woh kya karne wale hain aur kyun, aur tum unhe pause ya stop karne ke liye bol sakte ho. Tumhari responsibility honesty hai: poori history do, woh parts bhi jinhe tum skip karna chahte ho.

body.en: Doctors and counsellors are expected to keep what you tell them private, and you can ask first, 'Who will this be shared with?' There are honest limits. If you are under 18, the law (POCSO) requires anyone who learns of sexual abuse or sexual activity involving a minor to report it, so no doctor, teacher or counsellor can promise total secrecy about that. They may also involve others if your life is at risk. For those under 18, a parent or guardian is usually needed to consent to treatment. This is not a reason to avoid care. It is a reason to ask how your information will be handled.
body.hg: Doctors aur counsellors se expect kiya jata hai ki tum jo batao use woh private rakhein, aur tum shuru mein hi pooch sakte ho, 'Yeh baat kis-kis ke saath share hogi?' Iski kuch honest limits hain. Agar tum 18 se kam ho, toh law (POCSO) ke hisaab se jise bhi kisi minor ke saath sexual abuse ya sexual activity ka pata chale, use report karna hota hai, isliye koi bhi doctor, teacher ya counsellor is baare mein total secrecy ka promise nahi kar sakta. Agar tumhari life ko risk ho, tab bhi woh doosron ko involve kar sakte hain. 18 se kam walon ke treatment ke consent ke liye usually parent ya guardian ki zaroorat hoti hai. Yeh care avoid karne ka reason nahi hai. Yeh is baat ka reason hai ki tum poocho ki tumhari information kaise handle hogi.

h.en: Parents, and a friend in trouble
h.hg: Parents, aur mushkil mein pada dost

body.en: For a hard talk at home, pick a calm time and say what you need: 'Papa, please listen for five minutes before you react.' State the facts, your feeling and the help you want. A first reaction often passes; try again tomorrow. If you fear being hurt or thrown out, start with another trusted adult, a counsellor or a helpline. When a friend confides, listen, believe them and say, 'Thank you for telling me. It's not your fault. What would help?' Do not investigate or spread it. If they are being harmed or thinking of self-harm, do not promise secrecy; help them reach an adult or 1098, 181 or 14416.
body.hg: Ghar pe kisi mushkil baat ke liye calm time choose karo aur shuruaat is baat se karo ki tumhe kya chahiye: 'Papa, please react karne se pehle paanch minute meri baat suniye.' Facts batao, apni feeling batao aur woh help batao jo tum chahte ho. Pehla reaction aksar guzar jata hai; agle din phir try karo. Agar tumhe darr hai ki baat chhedne pe tumhe hurt kiya jayega ya ghar se nikaal diya jayega, toh shuruaat kisi doosre trusted adult, counsellor ya helpline se karo. Jab koi dost tumhare saamne open up kare, toh poori baat suno, uspe believe karo aur bolo, 'Mujhe batane ke liye thank you. Isme tumhari galti nahi hai. Kis cheez se help milegi?' Investigate mat karo aur baat phailao mat. Agar use harm kiya ja raha hai ya woh self-harm ka soch raha hai, toh secret rakhne ka promise mat karo; use kisi adult tak ya 1098, 181 ya 14416 tak pahunchne mein help karo.

claim.en: If I tell the doctor the whole truth about my body or habits, they will judge me or refuse to treat me.
claim.hg: Agar main doctor ko apni body ya habits ke baare mein poora sach bata dun, toh woh mujhe judge karenge ya treat karne se mana kar denge.

fact.en: A doctor's job is to treat, not to judge, and accurate information is what makes the treatment right. If a doctor shames you, that is poor practice, and you are entitled to see a different one.
fact.hg: Doctor ka kaam treat karna hai, judge karna nahi, aur accurate information se hi treatment sahi hota hai. Agar koi doctor tumhe shame kare, toh woh poor practice hai, aur tumhe kisi doosre doctor ko dikhane ka poora haq hai.

takeaways.en: Write down your symptoms, dates and questions before an appointment, and use plain body words.
takeaways.hg: Appointment se pehle apne symptoms, dates aur sawaal likh lo, aur body ke seedhe words use karo.

takeaways.en: Confidentiality is the rule but has limits, and nobody can promise a person under 18 total secrecy about sexual abuse or sexual activity.
takeaways.hg: Confidentiality rule hai par uski limits hain, aur 18 se kam age ke insaan ko sexual abuse ya sexual activity ke baare mein total secrecy ka promise koi nahi kar sakta.

takeaways.en: With a friend in trouble: listen, believe, ask what helps, and connect them to an adult or helpline when there is harm.
takeaways.hg: Mushkil mein pade dost ke saath: suno, believe karo, poocho kisse help milegi, aur harm ki baat ho toh use kisi adult ya helpline se connect karo.

activity.en: Fill in a 'visit card' for yourself, even if you are not ill: your known allergies, regular medicines, past illnesses, and three questions you would ask at your next appointment. Keep it in your phone notes.
activity.hg: Apne liye ek 'visit card' bharo, bhale hi tum bimaar na ho: tumhari known allergies, regular medicines, purani illnesses, aur teen sawaal jo tum next appointment pe poochoge. Isse apne phone ke notes mein rakho.

q.en: A friend tells you about a serious problem at home. What is the most helpful first response?
q.hg: Ek dost tumhe ghar ki ek serious problem ke baare mein batata hai. Sabse helpful first response kya hoga?

options.en: 'Are you sure? That doesn't sound like your family.'
options.hg: 'Pakka? Tumhari family toh aisi nahi lagti.'

options.en: Share it with two close friends to get advice
options.hg: Advice lene ke liye do close friends ko bata do

options.en: Tell them exactly what they must do
options.hg: Use exactly bata do ki use kya karna hi hai

options.en: 'Thank you for telling me. I believe you. What would help right now?'
options.hg: 'Mujhe batane ke liye thank you. Mujhe tumpe believe hai. Abhi kis cheez se help milegi?'

explain.en: Being believed and asked what they need keeps a friend talking. Doubt, gossip and instructions tend to shut them down.
explain.hg: Jab dost pe believe kiya jata hai aur poocha jata hai ki use kya chahiye, toh woh baat karta rehta hai. Doubt, gossip aur instructions use chup kara dete hain.

q.en: A school counsellor can promise a 16-year-old complete secrecy about sexual abuse.
q.hg: School counsellor 16 saal ke kisi teen ko sexual abuse ke baare mein complete secrecy ka promise kar sakta hai.

options.en: True
options.hg: Sahi

options.en: False
options.hg: Galat

explain.en: Under POCSO, anyone who learns of a sexual offence against a person under 18 must report it, so total secrecy cannot be promised.
explain.hg: POCSO ke under, jise bhi 18 se kam age ke kisi insaan ke against sexual offence ka pata chale, use report karna hota hai, isliye total secrecy ka promise nahi kiya ja sakta.

warning.en: This lesson does not replace medical advice. Severe pain, heavy bleeding, difficulty breathing, fainting or thoughts of self-harm need urgent care: call 112 or go to the nearest hospital.
warning.hg: Yeh lesson medical advice ki jagah nahi le sakta. Severe pain, heavy bleeding, saans lene mein takleef, behoshi ya self-harm ke thoughts hon toh turant care lo: 112 pe call karo ya sabse nazdeeki hospital jao.

title.en: Fact-Check Mode: Health Info You Can Trust

subtitle.en: Critical thinking, spotting fake health claims and behaving responsibly online
subtitle.hg: Critical thinking, fake health claims pakadna aur online responsibly behave karna

hook.en: A reel with ten million views can still be wrong. Popular and true are two different things.
hook.hg: Ek crore views wali reel bhi galat ho sakti hai. Popular hona aur sach hona do alag cheezein hain.

objectives.en: Explain why health misinformation spreads easily.
objectives.hg: Samjha sako ki health misinformation itni easily kyun phailti hai.

objectives.en: Apply five checks to any health claim and recognise the red flags of quackery.
objectives.hg: Kisi bhi health claim pe paanch checks laga sako aur quackery ke red flags pehchaan sako.
Responsibly post, forward aur comment kar sako.

h.hg: Galat information zyada fast kyun phailti hai

body.en: Platforms reward whatever people watch and share, not whatever is correct. Shocking, scary or 'secret' claims get more clicks than a careful explanation, so they travel further. Health topics that people feel shy about, such as periods, masturbation, body size, pregnancy and infections, are an easy market, because embarrassed people search privately instead of asking a doctor. Add family WhatsApp forwards, confident influencers and paid promotions that look like advice, and it becomes hard to tell knowledge from marketing. Critical thinking does not mean distrusting everything. It means asking for evidence before you believe, act or forward.
body.hg: Platforms usi cheez ko push karte hain jo log dekhte aur share karte hain, usko nahi jo correct hai. Shocking, scary ya 'secret' claims pe kisi careful explanation se zyada clicks aate hain, isliye woh zyada door tak pahunchte hain. Health ke woh topics jinpe logon ko sharam aati hai, jaise periods, masturbation, body size, pregnancy aur infections, ek easy market hain, kyunki embarrassed log doctor se poochne ki jagah privately search karte hain. Isme family WhatsApp forwards, confident influencers aur advice jaise dikhne wale paid promotions add kar do, toh knowledge aur marketing mein farak karna mushkil ho jata hai. Critical thinking ka matlab har cheez pe distrust karna nahi hai. Iska matlab hai believe karne, act karne ya forward karne se pehle evidence maangna.

h.en: Five checks for any health claim
h.hg: Kisi bhi health claim ke liye paanch checks

body.en: Who is saying it? Look for a named, qualified source: a registered doctor, a hospital, a government health programme or the World Health Organization. What is the evidence? Good sources explain how they know and admit what is uncertain. Why was it made? If it ends with 'buy this' or 'DM for the course', treat it as an advertisement. When was it written? Medical advice is updated, so check the date. Does anyone else agree? Compare with at least two independent, reliable sources. An answer from a search engine or an AI chatbot is a starting point for a question to a professional. It is not a diagnosis.
body.hg: Kaun bol raha hai? Naam wala, qualified source dhoondo: koi registered doctor, hospital, government health programme ya World Health Organization. Evidence kya hai? Achhe sources batate hain ki unhe yeh kaise pata hai, aur yeh bhi maante hain ki kya abhi uncertain hai. Yeh kyun banaya gaya? Agar end mein 'yeh kharido' ya 'course ke liye DM karo' aata hai, toh isse ad samjho. Yeh kab likha gaya? Medical advice update hoti rehti hai, isliye date check karo. Kya koi aur bhi yahi bolta hai? Kam se kam do independent, reliable sources se compare karo. Search engine ya AI chatbot ka answer kisi professional se sawaal poochne ka starting point bhar hai. Woh diagnosis nahi hai.

body.en: Be suspicious of 'guaranteed', '100 percent cure' or 'results in seven days'; of one product that claims to fix many unrelated problems; of 'doctors don't want you to know this'; of before-and-after photos and testimonials offered instead of studies; and of wall posters or online ads promising to cure 'sexual weakness', increase height or body-part size, or 'tighten' or 'whiten' anything. 'Natural', 'herbal' and 'ayurvedic' do not automatically mean safe; any product strong enough to act can also have side effects, and a label does not always list everything inside. Never take prescription medicines, hormones or leftover antibiotics on a friend's or a video's advice.
body.hg: In cheezon pe shak karo: 'guaranteed', '100 percent cure' ya 'saat din mein result'; ek hi product jo kai unrelated problems fix karne ka claim kare; 'doctors nahi chahte ki tumhe yeh pata chale'; studies ki jagah before-after photos aur testimonials; aur deewar ke posters ya online ads jo 'gupt rog' ya 'kamzori' theek karne, height ya kisi body part ka size badhane, ya kuch bhi 'tight' ya 'gora' karne ka promise karein. 'Natural', 'herbal' aur 'ayurvedic' ka matlab automatically safe nahi hota; jo cheez asar karne jitni strong hai uske side effects bhi ho sakte hain, aur label pe hamesha andar ki har cheez likhi nahi hoti. Kisi dost ya video ke kehne pe kabhi bhi prescription medicines, hormones ya bachi hui antibiotics mat lo.

body.en: You are also a source. Before you post or forward, pause on three questions: Is it true? Is it mine to share? Could it hurt someone? Do not forward unverified health tips, rumours about a classmate or screenshots of private chats. Ask before posting a photo that has someone else in it. Disagree with ideas without attacking the person, and do not pile on when a comment section turns on somebody. Remember that messages can be saved and shared long after you delete them. If you shared something false, correct it in the same group. That takes thirty seconds, and more courage than most people show online.
body.hg: Tum khud bhi ek source ho. Post ya forward karne se pehle teen sawaalon pe ruko: Kya yeh sach hai? Kya isse share karna mera haq hai? Kya isse kisi ko hurt ho sakta hai? Bina verify kiye health tips, kisi classmate ke baare mein rumours ya private chats ke screenshots forward mat karo. Jis photo mein koi aur bhi ho, use post karne se pehle pooch lo. Ideas se disagree karo, par insaan pe attack mat karo, aur jab comment section kisi ek ke peeche pad jaye toh bheed mein shaamil mat ho. Yaad rakho ki tumhare delete karne ke bahut baad tak bhi messages save aur share kiye ja sakte hain. Agar tumne kuch galat share kar diya, toh usi group mein use correct karo. Isme tees second lagte hain, aur usse zyada himmat jitni zyadatar log online dikhate hain.

claim.en: If a remedy is natural or herbal, it cannot harm you.
claim.hg: Agar koi remedy natural ya herbal hai, toh usse nuksaan nahi ho sakta.

fact.en: Natural products can cause side effects, allergies and interactions with other medicines, and the dose matters. 'Natural' describes where something comes from, not how safe it is. Ask a qualified doctor or pharmacist before using any remedy for a health problem.
fact.hg: Natural products se bhi side effects, allergies aur doosri medicines ke saath interactions ho sakte hain, aur dose bhi matter karti hai. 'Natural' yeh batata hai ki cheez kahan se aayi hai, yeh nahi ki woh kitni safe hai. Health ki kisi problem ke liye koi bhi remedy use karne se pehle kisi qualified doctor ya pharmacist se poocho.

takeaways.en: Views and forwards measure attention, not accuracy.
takeaways.hg: Views aur forwards attention measure karte hain, accuracy nahi.

takeaways.en: Check who, what evidence, why, when, and whether reliable sources agree.
takeaways.hg: Check karo kaun bol raha hai, evidence kya hai, kyun, kab, aur kya reliable sources agree karte hain.

takeaways.en: Before you post or forward, ask whether it is true, yours to share and harmless.
takeaways.hg: Post ya forward karne se pehle poocho ki kya yeh sach hai, kya isse share karna tumhara haq hai, aur kya isse kisi ko harm nahi hoga.

activity.en: Pick one health claim from your feed or a family group this week. Run the five checks on it and write a one-line verdict: trustworthy, unproven or false. Do not forward it while you are checking.
activity.hg: Is week apni feed ya family group se ek health claim choose karo. Uspe paanchon checks lagao aur ek line ka verdict likho: trustworthy, unproven ya false. Jab tak check kar rahe ho, use forward mat karo.

q.en: Which of these is the strongest warning sign in a health advertisement?
q.hg: Kisi health ad mein inme se sabse bada warning sign kaun-sa hai?

options.en: It names the doctor and the hospital
options.hg: Usme doctor aur hospital ka naam diya hai

options.en: It says results vary from person to person
options.hg: Usme likha hai ki results har insaan mein alag ho sakte hain

options.en: It promises a guaranteed cure in seven days
options.hg: Woh saat din mein guaranteed cure ka promise karta hai

options.en: It advises you to consult your own doctor
options.hg: Woh tumhe apne doctor se consult karne ko bolta hai

explain.en: Honest medicine does not guarantee outcomes or fixed timelines. The other three are signs of a more careful source.
explain.hg: Honest medicine results ya fixed timeline ki guarantee nahi deti. Baaki teeno zyada careful source ke signs hain.

q.en: The date on a health article matters because medical advice gets updated.
q.hg: Health article ki date matter karti hai kyunki medical advice update hoti rehti hai.

options.en: True
options.hg: Sahi

options.en: False
options.hg: Galat

explain.en: Recommendations change as new evidence comes in, so an old article may no longer reflect current guidance.
explain.hg: Naye evidence aane pe recommendations badalti hain, isliye ho sakta hai purana article aaj ki guidance se match na kare.
